{{Short description|American biologist}}
'''Richard Malcolm Brown Jr.''' (Born January 2nd 1939)<ref name="Dignity_Memorial-1">{{Cite web |title=Richard Brown Obituary - Austin, TX |url=https://www.dignitymemorial.com/obituaries/austin-tx/richard-brown-12674473 |access-date=2026-11-03 |website=Dignity Memorial |language=en-us}}</ref> was an American [[biologist]] and [[Botany|botanist]] who served as the [[Johnson & Johnson]] centennial chair in plant cell biology at [[University of Texas at Austin]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://tmi.utexas.edu/tmi-people/r-malcolm-brown/ |title=R. Malcolm Brown |publisher=utexas.edu |accessdate=December 13, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://catalog.utexas.edu/undergraduate/natural-sciences/faculty/ |title=Faculty |publisher=utexas.edu |accessdate=December 13, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.botany.utexas.edu/Mbrownhome/ |title=R M Brown |publisher=utexas.edu |accessdate=December 13, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.worldcat.org/identities/lccn-n82028469/ |title=Brown, R. Malcolm |publisher=worldcat.org |accessdate=December 13, 2016}}</ref> Dr. Brown attended the University of Texas at Austin and studied under [[Harold Charles Bold|Dr. Harold C. Bold]].<ref name="Dignity_Memorial-1" /> Dr. Brown majored in botany and received his PhD in Botany in 1964 before joining the UT Austin faculty as an assistant professor in 1965.<ref name="Dignity_Memorial-1" /> Dr. Brown began teaching at the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]] in 1968 as an associate professor, and was promoted to a full professor in 1973.<ref name="Dignity_Memorial-1" /> Dr. Brown returned to UT Austin in  1982 to serve as the inaugural holder of the Johnson & Johnson Centennial Endowed Chair in Plant Biology.<ref name="Dignity_Memorial-1" /> Dr. Richard Malcolm Brown Jr. died on December 20th, 2025 at the age of 86.<ref name="Dignity_Memorial-1" />
